steps.description: Parse binary STL file — read header, triangle normals/vertices, and Attribute Byte Count for Material ID

failure_patterns.reason: ⚠️ Do not use trimesh/numpy-stl to load the file — the Material ID is stored in Attribute Byte Count (bytes 80-81 of each triangle), which these libraries discard. Parse the binary format directly with struct.unpack.

suggestions: Binary STL layout: 80-byte header, 4-byte uint32 triangle count, then per-triangle: 12 floats (normal + 3 vertices) + 2-byte attribute (Material ID).
Read Material ID: struct.unpack('<H', f.read(2))[0] after reading each triangle's normal and vertices.
warnings: The Attribute Byte Count (2 bytes after each triangle) contains the Material ID — do NOT skip it.

steps.description: Build triangle adjacency graph by shared edges to identify connected components

suggestions: Two triangles are adjacent if they share an edge (any 2 of their 3 vertices are identical).
Use Union-Find (disjoint sets) for efficient connectivity: union triangles that share any edge.

steps.description: Identify and keep the largest connected component — discard scanning debris

suggestions: Group triangles by component ID, then keep the group with the most triangles.

steps.description: Compute mesh volume using signed volume formula over all triangles in the main component

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ Do not use bounding box volume — compute true mesh volume using the signed volume (divergence) formula: V = sum(v1 · (v2 × v3)) / 6.

suggestions: Signed volume per triangle: V_i = v0 · (v1 × v2) / 6. Sum V_i and take abs(sum) for total mesh volume.

steps.description: Look up material density from material_density_table.md using the extracted Material ID

suggestions: Read material_density_table.md to find the density (g/cm³) for the Material ID from the STL.

steps.description: Compute mass = volume × density (with correct unit conversions) and save to mass_report.json

suggestions: Convert volume from mm³ to cm³ (divide by 1000) before multiplying by density in g/cm³. Save mass in grams to mass_report.json.
